study_identification_part.si4_title: Patterns of connectome variability in autism across five functional activation tasks: findings from the LEAP project

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract and introduction clearly state the study's aims: to characterize heterogeneity in autism by identifying patterns of neural diversity across multiple task-fMRI paradigms, using task potency and normative modeling, and to relate individual-level atypicality to behavioral measures via robust out-of-sample CCA. This satisfies both criteria: explicit research questions/purpose and the rationale for applying normative modeling.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "our goal was to characterize heterogeneity in autism by identifying patterns of neural diversity as reflected in BOLD fMRI ..."; "Normative modelling was used to map atypicality of features on an individual basis ... We applied robust out-of-sample canonical correlation analysis (CCA) to relate connectome data to behavioral data."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: A new normative model was built from TD participants. The paper describes eligibility criteria and image/data quality standards (IQ ≥ 75; registration overlap thresholds; exclusion for poor atlas overlap; incidental findings; incomplete scans; high motion), reports final sample sizes, and notes reasons for exclusion. These satisfy all criteria for NEW normative models.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "Data from participants with intellectual disability (IQ < 75) were not included ..."; "excluded 57 participants due to poor overlap (< 50%) with one or more particular regions ..."; "excluded on the basis of incidental findings and incomplete scans (N = 18), and those in the top 5% in terms of head motion ... (N = 27)"; "inclusion of data ... 282 participants with autism ... and 221 typically developing controls ..."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex are explicitly modeled in the normative model. The dataset is multi-site, and site effects are addressed using ComBat to clean linear site effects during preprocessing. This meets both covariate and multi-site handling criteria.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "A normative model of potency edge values was built against age and sex ... using the nispat implementation in python"; "ComBat was used to clean the data for linear site effects [39]."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The reference cohort data source is clearly specified as the EU-AIMS/AIMS-2-TRIALS LEAP project, with collection sites listed and pointers to methods/clinical characterization papers.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The dataset from the EU-AIMS/AIMS2TRIALS LEAP project was used ..."; "MRI data were acquired on 3T scanners at multiple sites in Europe—King's College London (KCL), Radboud University Nijmegen Medical Centre (RUNMC), University Medical Centre Utrecht (UMCU), Autism Research Centre (ARC), University of Cambridge (UCAM), Central Institute of Mental Health, Mannheim (CIMH) ..."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Secondary data (existing LEAP dataset) were used; per guidance, image acquisition protocol is not applicable for secondary datasets, even though parameters are provided in the supplement.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing steps and software (FSL) are detailed, including motion correction (MCFLIRT), smoothing, ICA-AROMA denoising, WM/CSF regression, high-pass filtering, registrations (FLIRT/FNIRT), atlas to native space, and ComBat for site effects. QC procedures include motion exclusion and registration overlap checks in the Sample section.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "Preprocessing ... was performed with tools from FSL ... volume realignment ... MCFLIRT ... smoothing ... ICA-AROMA ... white matter and cerebrospinal fluid was regressed out ... 0.01 Hz high-pass ... registrations ... FLIRT ... FNIRT ... ComBat was used to clean the data for linear site effects ..."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: They state the normative model was used to predict edge-value ranges in out-of-sample TD and autistic participants, implying a partitioning or cross-validation strategy. However, explicit details of the partitioning scheme (e.g., K-fold, LOOCV, hold-out sizes) are not described for the normative model itself.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "The model was used to predict the range of (a)typical edge values in out-of-sample typically developing participants as well as the autistic participants."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: No independent external dataset of healthy individuals was used to validate the normative model; all analyses are within the LEAP cohort.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: No mention of application to an independent external healthy control dataset; all data described are from LEAP.

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: They specify covariates (age, sex), implementation (nispat in Python), and the transformation to Z-scores with an extreme-value threshold. However, the exact statistical model class (e.g., Gaussian process regression vs. linear model) and key settings (e.g., kernel, priors, smoothing) are not described.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "A normative model of potency edge values was built against age and sex ... using the nispat implementation in python ... Task potency values were thereby transformed to Z-scores ... thresholding the Z-scores at z = |±2.571| ..."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: The paper does not report quantitative fit/calibration metrics for the normative model on the reference cohort (e.g., explained variance, prediction error, coverage of prediction intervals). Analyses focus on deviation Z-scores and group differences rather than model performance in TD.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: No explained-variance, error, or coverage metrics are reported for the normative model; only Z-score derivations and downstream analyses are described.

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: While out-of-sample prediction is mentioned, the study does not detail the sizes or demographic characteristics of partitions (training/validation/test) specific to the normative model. Subsample characterizations per task are provided but not broken down by normative model partitions.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: "... out-of-sample ..." (normative model) without partition details; Supplementary tables describe task subsamples, not model partitions.

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Software used is identified (FSL for preprocessing; nispat in Python for normative modeling), and the data source is cited (LEAP). However, software/library versions are not specified, and there is no statement about code, trained model availability, or data access conditions beyond the LEAP citations.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: "Preprocessing ... performed with tools from FSL ..."; "using the nispat implementation in python"; "The dataset from the EU-AIMS/AIMS2TRIALS LEAP project was used ..."

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: Secondary clinical data from LEAP were used with citation of the original project papers. Additional eligibility and QC criteria applied in this study are described (IQ cutoff, registration overlap, atlas overlap, incidental findings, incomplete scans, high motion), along with final sample sizes and reasons for exclusion.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "The dataset from the EU-AIMS/AIMS2TRIALS LEAP project was used ..."; "Data from participants with intellectual disability (IQ < 75) were not included ... excluded 57 ... incidental findings and incomplete scans (N = 18) ... top 5% ... head motion (N = 27) ... 282 participants with autism ... and 221 typically developing controls ..."

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses of deviation patterns incorporate clinical covariates beyond demographics by relating brain atypicality to multiple clinical/behavioral measures (SRS, RBS, SSP, ADHD subscales, Vineland, IQ) using CCA.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: "Total scores on seven behavioral variables were included ... SRS ... RBS ... SSP ... ADHD hyperactivity/impulsivity ... ADHD inattentiveness ... Vineland ... IQ ..."; "We applied robust out-of-sample CCA to relate connectome data to behavioral data."

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: The clinical cohort data source is specified as LEAP, with participating sites listed and references to the LEAP clinical characterization and methods papers.
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "The dataset from the EU-AIMS/AIMS2TRIALS LEAP project was used ..."; "MRI data were acquired on 3T scanners at multiple sites ... KCL ... RUNMC ... UMCU ... ARC ... UCAM ... CIMH ..."

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: Sample sizes are reported for ASD and TD overall; subsample characterizations per task include demographics (age, sex implicitly via cohort descriptions) and clinical measures (e.g., SRS, RBS, SSP, ADHD scales, Vineland, IQ) in the supplement tables.
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: "... 282 participants with autism ... and 221 typically developing controls ..."; Supplementary Tables S1–S5 report age, IQ, SRS, RBS, SSP, ADHD subscales, Vineland per task.

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: The study specifies the clinical/behavioral measures used (SRS, RBS, SSP, DSM-5 ADHD rating scale components, Vineland, IQ) with citations.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: "Social Responsiveness Scale-2 (SRS) ... Repetitive Behaviors Scale-revised (RBS) ... Short Sensory Profile (SSP) ... ADHD hyperactivity/impulsivity, and ADHD inattentiveness ... Vineland-II Adaptive Behavior Composite (Vineland) ... Full scale intelligence quotient (IQ) ..."

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: They define deviation scores as Z-scores from a normative model and set a quantitative threshold (|Z| ≥ 2.571) to identify atypical edges, and they discuss clinical relevance by linking atypicality patterns to behavior via significant CCA. However, explicit interpretation of the sign/direction of deviation per edge is not detailed.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: "Task potency values were thereby transformed to Z-scores quantifying the atypicality per edge ... Percentage of connectome deemed atypical was identified by thresholding the Z-scores at z = |±2.571| ..."; "The CCA identified significant and robust brain-behavior covariation between functional connectivity atypicality and autism-related behavioral features."
